subject: Cutover sanity check: lights-on & smoke results
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jose Sanchez <j.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Cutover sanity check: lights-on & smoke results

Team / Jose,

Thanks again for the smooth window last night — we completed the private VPC switch and the core control-plane handoff to Acme's edge fabric. This thread is to capture the immediate post-cutover sanity pass and list next actions for the first 48 hours. Attached: runbook_v2.pdf, vpc_topology_v3.png.

Quick summary (pass/fail highlights):
- Control plane registration: PASS (all hosts reported in the control-plane registry).
- KV cache priming: PARTIAL (cold miss rate higher than expected on first 5 minutes).
- Ingress health-checks: PASS at L7; two transient 503s correlated to NAT gateway flaps at 02:14 UTC.
- Observability pipes: PASS (logs and traces are flowing to the retention tier).

Immediate asks (owners):
1) Mateo: Please attach the smoke CSV and a short note on kv-priming steps you executed.
2) Monica: Pull the p95 latency numbers per region for the first hour and flag any >300ms spikes.
3) Rishi: Confirm that we captured the required audit events for the Private deployment compliance checklist (SOC2 items 3.1–3.4).
4) Jose / Acme: If you see any functional failures on your side, paste a minimal repro here — we won't roll back proactively unless there is a customer-impacting failure.

We should aim to keep this thread tight: short status updates, any blocking items, and clear go/no-go for a partial rollback if impact is customer-visible.

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Systems PM, Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jose Sanchez <j.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 10:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Cutover sanity check: lights-on & smoke results

Sofia — quick update, attaching smoke_results_20280112.csv (small attachment).

What we ran: a 30-min staged traffic primer across two availability zones, hitting the primary model endpoint and the fallback variant. Steps executed:
- KV priming: warmed prefixes sequentially (low -> med -> high throughput) using the primer agent.
- Retrying policy: 2 retries on 5xx with exponential backoff (50ms -> 200ms).
- Traffic shaping: initial concurrency capped at 40 RPS, increased to 250 RPS over 20 minutes.

Observations:
- Cold-miss window lasted ~4 minutes; cold-miss rate dropped from 38% to 2% after sequential prefix priming.
- Two NAT gateway flaps correlated to a BGP flibber from the edge provider during the 02:10–02:16 UTC window; we saw short-lived 503s but automatic retries recovered.
- No model-serving OOMs or GPU preemption observed.

Action items I completed: attached CSV + a short log snippet in the Drive link. I'll follow up with a short KV priming tweak (increase inter-prefix concurrency) and re-run the primer in the quiet window tonight.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Platform Engineer, Inference Serving

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jose Sanchez <j.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Cutover sanity check: lights-on & smoke results

On Fri, Jan 12, 2028 at 10:18 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sofia — quick update, attaching smoke_results_20280112.csv (small attachment).
>
> What we ran: a 30-min staged traffic primer ...

Attached: smoke_results_20280112.csv (summary below).

Metrics (first 60 minutes, aggregated):
- Total requests: 48,320
- 2xx: 48,100
- 5xx: 220 (mostly 503 gateway during 02:10–02:16 UTC)
- p50: 38ms, p95: 235ms, p99: 610ms (p99 spike coincided with NAT flap + a few long tail KV cache misses)
- Error surface: 70% of 5xx were transient gateway errors; 30% were downstream load-balancer configuration mismatch for one edge node (node id: edge-az2-17).

Notes / recommendations:
- Short term: apply the LB config fix to edge-az2-17 and re-prime KV for the node. Estimated 15–25 minutes.
- Medium term: increase the KV priming concurrency as Mateo suggested; roll a tiny routing policy tweak to reduce burst pressure on NAT gateways.
- Compliance: audit events for role-change and deployment artifacts have been captured and archived to the Acme shared folder (link above). Rishi, please confirm retention window matches Acme's requirement.

I'll push a one-line postmortem into the Drive doc after the LB fix.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jose Sanchez <j.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeCloud Sales <sales@edgecloud.io>
Date: Sat, 13 Jan 2028 07:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Cutover sanity check: lights-on & smoke results

Thanks Sofia — quick note from our side. Around 02:12 UTC the Acme internal dashboard logged a 502 -> 503 cascade for one shard serving our realtime inference. Minimal repro below:
- Request: POST /v1/generate 
- Payload: {"prompt":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":64}
- Response: 503 Service Unavailable (x-redwood-error: upstream-gateway)

We saw ~4 user sessions affected; one customer reported a failure in a critical path. We are fine with the LB fix and re-prime approach as long as we get confirmation when it's completed and a short RCA. Not requesting rollback at this time — prefer mitigation and targeted fix.

Jose Sanchez
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Corp.

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jose Sanchez <j.sanchez@acme-corp.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, EdgeCloud Sales <sales@edgecloud.io>
Date: Sat, 14 Jan 2028 16:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Cutover sanity check: lights-on & smoke results

Jose — thanks for the repro and context. Closing the loop:
- Monica applied the LB config patch to edge-az2-17 at 13:20 UTC on 2028-01-13; we observed error rates drop to baseline within ~4 minutes.
- Mateo re-ran the KV priming with increased concurrency at 20:00 UTC (same day); cold-miss rate went from 2% -> 0.4% and p99 dropped to 320ms on the subsequent run.
- Rishi confirmed the audit bundle and retention metadata match Acme's SOC2 evidence requirements; artifacts moved to https://drive.redwood/reports/ACME-Cutover-20280112 and flagged JIRA OPS-1742 for a short-term ticket to harden NAT gateway resiliency.

Next steps and closure:
- We will keep a staggered primer every 12 hours for 48 hours and report p99 and 5xx counts in this thread.
- Monica to post a 1-page postmortem in Drive by EOD Monday outlining root cause and mitigations.
- If any functional impact >1% or sustained for >10 minutes occurs, we will initiate the rollback play (runbook_v2.pdf, section 4).

Thanks everyone for the quick triage — tagging this as operationally closed for now; will reopen if new issues surface.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Systems PM, Redwood Inference
